note: Sixth edition (G-84). Two changes, both from running twenty-five real scenarios through the fifth and reading what came out. Confidential data on its own no longer lifts a band: nearly all enterprise work is confidential, so a floor that fires on it alone put fifteen of twenty-five scenarios at High and stopped sorting anything. It now lifts in combination — with AI, with a company outside ours, or at the top classification alone. And the floor can see sensitive information that is not about people: a pricing algorithm, privileged material or an unpublished filing leaving the boundary now rates the way customer data does. Before this an AI assistant on the pricing engine reached High only because its requester happened to tick Restricted rather than Confidential.

residual.note: Starts at the inherent band and can only fall. A step is never positive — the engine refuses an edition that tries — because a control cannot make an activity riskier than it is before any control exists. A fall has to be earned by evidence: an assessment that required no control at all has demonstrated nothing and stays where it is. An unfinished assessment earns nothing back either. A promised fix is a plan, not a control, and earns nothing until a reviewer settles the finding again to say it is done. The zero steps are the reasons nothing was earned back, and they are shown as such — including the commonest one of all, a control still waiting for a signature, which the second edition left the screen silent about.
